title: Hemoglobin electrophoresis (thalassemia)
what: This blood test shows which types of hemoglobin are in your blood and how much of each. It finds inherited traits like thalassemia.
why: If your red blood cells are small but your iron is normal, if inherited anemia runs in the family, and before or during pregnancy.
duration: the blood draw usually takes 5 minutes; results usually come in a few days
tell_doctor: If you had a blood transfusion in the last 3 months
If you are low in iron or take iron
If relatives have anemia or thalassemia

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: You usually do not need to fast. If you are having other tests at the same time, check with the lab.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop anything on your own, including iron. Just tell your doctor what you take.

bring: Past complete blood counts and iron tests
steps: You sit down, and a band is tied above your elbow
The skin is wiped with antiseptic
Blood is taken from a vein into a tube
The band is removed, and a cotton pad is pressed on the spot
feel: A quick prick, like a pinch
Sometimes slight dizziness. Tell the nurse, and they will help you lie down
after: Press the cotton pad for 3 to 5 minutes
Results usually come in a few days
If you are found to be a carrier, the doctor may suggest testing your partner and relatives

faq.q: Is being a thalassemia carrier an illness?
faq.a: Usually not. Carriers live like everyone else, sometimes with mild anemia. It matters when planning children.
Only if you really are low in iron. Your doctor decides. Too much iron can do harm.

reminders.text: Hemoglobin types test tomorrow. Bring your past blood test results.
